text: The service queuing system was terrible. I waited in the reception area for an hour, then the assistant called my number to sit at the dental chair. I waited another 15 minutes before the dentist finished serving the patients before me. Just as the dentist was about to serve me, they continued discussing their dental case (the rooms were connected, so I could hear). Eventually, the patient asked the dentist to proceed with the scaling, which would add another half hour. The dentist tried to refuse somewhat, but their reasoning was probably weak. In the end, the dentist agreed to proceed with that patient's scaling. There was only one dentist while two other patients were waiting. I urge the dentist to be more firm in refusing the patient and to show more consideration for the waiting patients. Because of this, I decided to leave the dental chair immediately. I don't know if the dentist's service was good or not, but even though this clinic is near my home, I will not go back. My experience was ruined. When I left the room, I complained loudly and was a little upset. The staff at the counter told me, "It's okay." At the time, I was irritated and didn't react, but now that I think about it, I want to say... You should say "I'm sorry" to us instead. "It's okay" should be our response if we truly feel that way.
